content:
maddy: Heads-up — hitting a parity issue between the JS SDK and the REST API in our onboarding sample app. SDK is silently retrying 401s and causing duplicate DB writes.

sam: ouch. do we know which retry policy triggered it?

maddy: looks like SDK default retry logic treats 401 as transient if it comes back with a short Retry-After. REST client (curl) returns 401 and we treat it as fatal. example: `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $OLD_TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> 401 no-retry.

caroline: can you paste the SDK call? maybe different param name or header?

maddy: using node sdk v0.12: `client.generate({ model: 'redwood/gpt-medium', input: prompt, maxTokens: 256 })` — note param is `maxTokens` in SDK. REST expects `max_tokens`. suspicion: SDK translates + triggers extra code path that enables safe-retry header.

sam: ah that param drift again. we had a mapping layer that normalizes camelCase -> snake_case, and it sets `x-sdk-retry: auto` when it does transform? that seems wrong.

devex-bot: deploy 1771209900: new SDK patch (v0.12.1) reverting auto-retry-on-transform.

maddy: tried v0.12.1 branch locally — better, but still seeing a retry when the auth header is missing for a split-second (refresh flow). the sampleapp does: fetch token -> call generate. if token refresh races, SDK retries once with an empty token because of a bug in the auth middleware.

kevin: is the sampleapp using the same auth middleware as customer apps?

maddy: yes, it's using the recommended snippet in docs: `authClient.attach(appClient)` — that wrapper used to be no-op on 401, but it now tries to refresh and re-invoke the call. refreshing is fine, but the first retry is fired before the refreshed token is attached.

caroline: two separate problems then: (1) param name mapping causing behavioural differences, (2) retry timing race in auth wrapper. both are DX regressions.

sam: proposed quick fixes: 1) SDK should not treat 401 as retriable by default — require opt-in via `retry.policy`. 2) Make auth middleware await refresh before re-invoking. 3) Add a linting test in sampleapp CI that compares SDK vs REST responses for the same request payload (including header parity).

maddy: wrote a failing unit test demonstrating REST vs SDK mismatch (attached gist): `expect(await restGenerate(body)).toEqual(await sdkGenerate(body))` — fails when body uses `max_tokens`.

kevin: can we add a warning in onboarding docs about param casing and current caveats until we ship patch?

caroline: yes, add a short note under "Quickstart -> Using the SDK" and link to the GH issue. I'll own the docs patch.

sam: filing a bug: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/542 — title: "SDK retries on 401 + param-name mapping causes duplicate side-effects in sampleapp". assigning to @eng-runtime.

maddy: TY. leaving the sampleapp disabled in demo flow until we get the hotfix out. :wave:

caroline: once the hotfix lands, let's add an e2e sample test that runs the demo flow with a mocked auth provider (to catch the race).

devex-bot: reminder in 24h: follow-up on #1771209876 - check SDK release notes.

sam: sounds good. if anyone sees other parity surprises (function-calling shape, streaming toggles), drop them here and we'll triage. :+1:
